intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus (Strætó) to Reykjavik BSÍ terminal (~45 min, ~3,500 ISK). Store luggage at BSÍ bus terminal locker while you explore Reykjavik before the long drive north.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a connecting bus from Reykjavik toward Siglufjörður (~5.5 hours drive via Route 1 and Route 76). Stop at Akureyri briefly to stretch legs and grab supplies at Bónus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest grocery chain). Continue north through the stunning Tröllaskagi peninsula to Siglufjörður, arriving by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check into Hotel Siglunes in Lækjargata 10. Settle in and take a short walk along the harbor front of Siglufjörður to get oriented. The town is tiny and charming — enjoy the quiet Arctic atmosphere. Watch for northern lights from the harbor after dark (darkness falls around 16:00 in January).

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure (~1,000 ISK) or pack snacks from home
meals.lunch: Stop at a gas station N1 or Orkan along Route 1 for a budget hot dog (pylsur) — Iceland's iconic cheap eat (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-cater from Bónus supermarket supplies purchased in Akureyri — pasta, canned soup, or bread and cheese in your hotel room (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January days are extremely short — only about 5 hours of daylight. Drive carefully on Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi peninsula as mountain roads can be icy. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. Northern lights visibility is high in Siglufjörður due to minimal light pollution.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, wake up and explore Siglufjörður town on foot. Visit the famous Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums documenting the town's herring boom era (~2,000 ISK entry). The museum is compact and fascinating, taking about 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or hike the short distance to the edge of town and explore the scenic fjord surroundings. Walk along the harbor breakwater for dramatic views of the snow-capped mountains surrounding the fjord. Visit the small local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a geothermally heated community pool, a true local experience (~1,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and prepare for northern lights hunting. Siglufjörður's location at 66°N makes it excellent for aurora viewing. Head to the harbor or a dark spot just outside town around 20:00–23:00. Download the Aurora Forecast app and aim for KP index 2 or higher.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or cereal from supermarket supplies in hotel room (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka café in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café with soup of the day and bread (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner — cook simple pasta with sauce using hotel kettle or microwave if available (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Siglufjörður is one of Iceland's most isolated and beautiful towns. January temperatures average around -2°C to 5°C here. Dress in warm layers. The swimming pool is a fantastic budget activity and a great way to meet locals.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike — the highlight experience available from the hotel area. Drive or walk to the tunnel entrance connecting Siglufjörður to Héðinsfjörður (the Héðinsfjarðargöng tunnel, free to use). Enter the completely uninhabited fjord and explore the hauntingly beautiful abandoned farmsteads. The landscape is dramatic and eerie in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Héðinsfjörður on foot. The fjord is completely uninhabited and offers raw, untouched Icelandic wilderness. Look for Arctic foxes, which are common in this area in winter. Take photos of the abandoned stone ruins against the snow-covered mountains. Return through the tunnel before darkness falls (around 16:00).
day_by_day.evening: Warm up at the Siglufjörður community pool or back at the hotel. Prepare a hot meal and rest. If skies are clear, set an alarm for midnight northern lights viewing from the hotel or harbor — January nights in Siglufjörður are among the best in Iceland for aurora activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — bread, cheese, and instant coffee from supermarket supplies (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — sandwiches, chocolate bars, and a thermos of hot tea or coffee from the hotel (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a meal at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — known for local fish dishes, order the catch of the day (~3,500 ISK for a main)

day_by_day.notes: Wear full winter hiking gear for Héðinsfjörður — waterproof boots, crampons or microspikes recommended for icy terrain. The tunnel is free but check it is open (it occasionally closes in severe weather). Carry a headlamp as daylight is very limited. This is a truly unique off-the-beaten-path experience.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður along the scenic Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi peninsula toward Hofsós (~1 hour). Stop at viewpoints along the dramatic coastal road. Visit the Hofsós Swimming Pool — arguably Iceland's most beautifully situated geothermal pool, perched on a cliff overlooking Skagafjörður fjord (~1,000 ISK). Soak in the hot pots with mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in Skagafjörður (~30 min from Hofsós). Browse the small town center and visit the local supermarket (Krónan or Nettó) to restock budget supplies. Drive back to Siglufjörður via the scenic mountain road (if conditions allow) or return via Route 76.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights watch from Siglufjörður harbor. The harbor area with the colorful fishing boats makes a beautiful foreground for aurora photography. Bring a tripod if you have one. Stay out until 22:00–23:00 if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — yogurt, granola, and coffee (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at a gas station or bakery in Sauðárkrókur — soup and bread (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — buy fresh fish from a local fishmonger in Sauðárkrókur and cook simply back at the hotel (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool is a must-do — it is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and costs a fraction of the price. Check road conditions before driving the mountain roads in January. Route 76 along the coast is generally well-maintained but can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akureyri — Iceland's second city (~1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 82 and Route 1). Arrive in Akureyri and walk the charming main street Hafnarstræti. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church (free entry) perched on the hill above town with panoramic views of Eyjafjörður fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri's budget-friendly attractions: the Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) is free and beautiful even in winter. Browse the local shops and visit the Bónus supermarket to stock up on budget groceries for the rest of the trip. Visit the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a large geothermal complex with hot tubs and slides (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður before full darkness if possible, or stay until early evening and drive carefully with headlights. The road through Öxnadalur valley is stunning. Northern lights watch upon return to Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — a beloved local institution with affordable soup and sandwiches (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered from Bónus supplies — make a hearty stew or soup back at the hotel (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great place to stock up on supplies and enjoy a slightly larger town atmosphere. The city has free WiFi in many cafés. Fuel up your rental car here as petrol is slightly cheaper in larger towns. Check aurora forecast for the evening drive back — you may see lights on the road.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the area around Siglufjörður more deeply. Drive or hike to the Siglufjörður ski area (Skíðasvæðið) — one of Iceland's oldest ski resorts located right above the town. Even without skiing, the views from the base area are spectacular. In January there is typically good snow cover.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex buildings — the museum complex includes a restored herring salting station and boat sheds along the harbor (included with Herring Era Museum ticket if you kept it). Spend time photographing the colorful harbor buildings and fishing boats reflected in the calm fjord water.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Drive 5–10 minutes out of town to completely escape light pollution. Park safely off the road and wait for aurora activity. Bring hot drinks in a thermos, warm blankets, and patience. January in northern Iceland offers some of the best aurora viewing in the world.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs (if hotel has microwave) or bread and peanut butter (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — try their homemade cake and coffee (~1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — canned fish (skyr, sardines) with rice and vegetables (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Siglufjörður ski area is a hidden gem — very affordable compared to European resorts if you want to ski (~5,000 ISK for a day pass). The northern lights are most active between 21:00 and 02:00. Set multiple alarms throughout the night to check conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east toward Dalvík and Ólafsfjörður (~45 min from Siglufjörður). Drive through the Strákagöng tunnel to Ólafsfjörður — another charming small fishing village. Walk the harbor and enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery. Visit the small local swimming pool in Ólafsfjörður (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Dalvík (~20 min from Ólafsfjörður). Dalvík is the departure point for whale watching tours in summer, but in January enjoy the peaceful harbor atmosphere. Visit the Hvoll Museum in Dalvík which includes a quirky exhibit on the world's tallest Icelander (free or small donation). Browse the local Samkaup supermarket for supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the tunnel. Rest and warm up. If energy allows, take a late evening walk along the harbor for northern lights viewing. The week is halfway through — reflect on the incredible landscapes experienced so far.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Gas station hot dog and coffee in Dalvík (~700 ISK) — the classic Icelandic budget meal
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to fish and chips or a burger at a local spot in Siglufjörður (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The tunnel roads connecting Siglufjörður, Ólafsfjörður, and Dalvík are free and make exploring the Tröllaskagi peninsula very accessible. These small fishing villages see very few tourists in January — you will have an authentic local experience. Dalvík has a small but well-stocked supermarket.

day_by_day.morning: Extended day trip to the Mývatn area (~2.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 1 east). Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. First stop: Goðafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most beautiful and accessible waterfalls, free to visit. The waterfall is dramatic in winter with ice formations along the edges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Lake Mývatn — a geologically unique volcanic lake. Visit the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pots, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents. Completely free to visit and otherworldly in winter. Drive around the lake to see the Dimmuborgir lava formations (free walking area).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a much more affordable and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon (~5,500 ISK). Soak in the milky blue geothermal waters surrounded by volcanic landscape. Drive back to Siglufjörður, watching for northern lights on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from hotel supplies to eat at Goðafoss or Mývatn (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant at Mývatn — a cozy local restaurant with affordable lamb soup (~2,500 ISK) before the drive back

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day — approximately 5 hours of driving total. Depart by 08:00 to make the most of daylight. The Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and offer a more authentic experience. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be challenging — check road.is. Carry an emergency kit in the car.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after the long Mývatn excursion. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Take a slow walk through Siglufjörður town, visiting the small local church and exploring the residential streets with their colorful corrugated iron houses — a quintessentially Icelandic architectural style.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a long, relaxing soak in the geothermal hot tubs (~1,000 ISK). This is a perfect way to warm up and relax muscles after days of hiking and driving. Chat with locals — Icelanders are friendly and the pool is a social hub.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated photography evening. Set up at the harbor with a camera or smartphone for long-exposure shots of the town lights reflecting on the fjord water. If northern lights appear, the harbor provides a beautiful foreground. Stay out until 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper café breakfast at Kaffi Rauðka — eggs, toast, and coffee (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Self-catered — skyr (Icelandic yogurt), fruit, and crackers (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty dinner — lamb stew made with supermarket ingredients (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important on a 13-day trip. Siglufjörður is a wonderful place to simply exist and absorb the Arctic atmosphere. The town has a small library that is free to visit. January sunsets (around 16:00) paint the fjord in extraordinary pink and orange hues — do not miss this.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip west to the Skagafjörður region. Drive to Varmahlíð (~1 hour from Siglufjörður). Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved traditional turf farmhouses (~2,000 ISK entry). The dark, low-ceilinged rooms give a vivid sense of how Icelanders lived for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sauðárkrókur for lunch and afternoon exploration. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) for more regional history (~1,500 ISK). Drive back toward Siglufjörður via the coastal Route 76, stopping at viewpoints over Skagafjörður — one of Iceland's widest fjords, famous for its horse breeding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by 17:00. Northern lights watch from the harbor or a dark spot outside town. January 25th statistically has good aurora probability — check the forecast carefully.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café in Sauðárkrókur — try the local bakery (Bakarí) for fresh bread and soup (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — buy fresh skyr and smoked lamb (hangikjöt) from supermarket for a traditional Icelandic dinner (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is one of Iceland's most authentic historical sites and well worth the entry fee. The Skagafjörður region is famous for Icelandic horse breeding — you may see herds of horses in the fields even in January. Hangikjöt (smoked lamb) is a traditional Icelandic food that is affordable and delicious.

day_by_day.morning: Final major excursion: drive to Akureyri and take the road south toward Aldeyjarfoss waterfall (~2 hours from Akureyri via the F26 highland road — check if accessible in January, may require 4WD). Alternatively, visit the Goðafoss area again for a different perspective in morning light. Goðafoss is free and stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eyjafjörður fjord area near Akureyri. Drive to Laufás — a historic turf farm on the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður with beautiful fjord views (may be closed in January but exterior is free to view). Drive back north toward Siglufjörður via the scenic Öxnadalur valley.
day_by_day.evening: Final major northern lights attempt. This is one of your last nights in the prime aurora viewing location. Set up at the best dark spot you have found during the trip. If you have not seen the aurora yet, tonight is the night to be most persistent — stay out until 01:00 if needed.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bónus supermarket in Akureyri — buy supplies and eat a simple lunch in the car (~800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your second-to-last dinner — Strikið restaurant in Akureyri has a budget lunch menu that sometimes extends to early dinner (~3,000 ISK) or self-cater back in Siglufjörður

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions carefully before attempting any F-roads in January — many highland roads are completely closed. The Öxnadalur valley drive is spectacular and safe year-round. This is your penultimate full day in the north — make the most of it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a last walk through the town you have come to know well. Visit any spots you missed — the small harbor chapel, the old fish factory ruins, the viewpoint above town. Pack your bags and check out of Hotel Siglunes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (~5.5 hours). Stop at Blönduós on Route 1 for a break and fuel. Continue through the dramatic Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau — a vast, windswept lava desert that feels like another planet. Stop at Borgarnes for a late afternoon break — visit the Settlement Center museum if budget allows (~2,500 ISK) or just walk the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik by early evening. Check into a budget hostel (Kex Hostel or Loft Hostel, ~5,000–7,000 ISK per night for a dorm). Walk the famous Laugavegur shopping street and Skólavörðustígur. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church exterior (free) illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast in Siglufjörður — use up remaining supplies (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: N1 gas station stop along Route 1 — hot dog and coffee (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Reykjavik budget dining: Hlöllabátar (Icelandic submarine sandwiches) on Laugavegur — filling and affordable (~1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik is long but beautiful. Depart by 09:00 to arrive in Reykjavik with time to explore. Book your Reykjavik hostel in advance. Reykjavik has excellent northern lights viewing from the Grótta lighthouse peninsula on the western edge of the city — check the forecast for your final night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early and walk to the Reykjavik Old Harbour (Grandi area) for sunrise views over the bay toward Mount Esja. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall exterior — a stunning glass building that is free to enter and photograph. Walk along the Sæbraut coastal path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free outdoor geothermal hot spring at Laugardalur — the Laugardalur swimming complex has hot tubs and is one of Reykjavik's best budget activities (~1,200 ISK). Alternatively, visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history (~2,500 ISK). Head to Keflavik Airport via Flybus (~3,500 ISK, departs BSÍ terminal).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of the Arctic north, northern lights, geothermal pools, and the hauntingly beautiful Héðinsfjörður. The flight home carries you away from one of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or self-catered from remaining supplies (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters café — excellent coffee and a pastry for a final Icelandic café experience (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Keflavik — budget option at the airport café or bring snacks from the city (~2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Flybus departs BSÍ terminal approximately 2.5 hours before flight departure — plan accordingly. Duty-free at Keflavik Airport is excellent for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs (Icelandic wool products, skyr, licorice). Budget tip: buy Icelandic wool lopapeysa sweaters at thrift stores (Kolaportið flea market on weekends) rather than tourist shops. Carry any remaining ISK as Iceland is largely cashless but some rural spots prefer card.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then arrange a pre-booked rental car or airport transfer. Begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður — approximately 4.5–5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Stop at a petrol station café near Akureyri for a break and fuel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north through the dramatic Tröllaskagi Peninsula, passing through the single-lane Strákagöng and Héðinsfjörðargöng tunnels. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early afternoon. Check in, unpack, and rest after the overnight flight. Take a gentle stroll along the harbour front to orient yourself with the town.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — head to Hannes Boy restaurant on the harbour for a warming bowl of lamb soup or fresh fish of the day. Return to the hotel early to recover from jet lag and prepare for the days ahead. Keep an eye on the northern lights forecast app (Vedur.is) before bed.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a petrol station café en route (Olis or N1 near Akureyri) — budget ~1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the airport or stop at Akureyri's Netto supermarket for sandwiches and drinks — budget ~2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant, Siglufjörður — fresh fish or lamb soup, mid-range main courses ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Given the 06:10 arrival and long drive, keep Day 1 very relaxed. January daylight in Siglufjörður is extremely limited (roughly 5 hours), so the drive will be partly in darkness — drive carefully on potentially icy roads. Download the Vedur.is app for weather and aurora forecasts. Stock up on groceries at Netto in Akureyri before heading into the fjords.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, spread across three restored warehouses on the harbour. Explore the fascinating exhibits on Siglufjörður's boom years as the herring capital of the North Atlantic, with reconstructed salting stations and period artefacts. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the compact town centre and explore the colourful wooden houses lining the fjord. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a classic Icelandic geothermal pool with hot pots, perfect for warming up and meeting locals. Spend 1–1.5 hours soaking and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — join a guided aurora tour departing from the town, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from any light pollution. The guide will find optimal viewing spots along the fjord edges and hillsides. Dress in maximum layers. Tour typically runs 2–3 hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast included or nearby Kaffi Rauðka café — skyr, eggs, and coffee ~2,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka on the main street — homemade soup and bread, a local favourite ~2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the aurora tour at Hannes Boy or pick up a hearty meal at the local grill — lamb burger or fish and chips ~3,000–4,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Book the northern lights tour in advance through the hotel or local operators. January offers the longest possible aurora-viewing windows (darkness from ~15:30 to ~10:30). The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — confirm opening times (typically 10:00–18:00 in summer, shorter in winter). Admission ~2,000 ISK per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 to Hofsós (approximately 45 minutes). Visit the stunning Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool — perched dramatically on a cliff edge above Skagafjörður with panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains. Arrive early to enjoy the pool before any crowds. Soak in the geothermally heated water while watching the winter light play across the fjord. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Hofsós, one of Iceland's oldest trading posts. Visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið) to learn about the thousands of Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century — a surprisingly moving and well-curated museum. Browse the small gift shop. Then drive back toward Siglufjörður, stopping at viewpoints along the fjord road.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Spend the evening at the hotel, reviewing aurora forecasts. If conditions look promising (KP index 3+, clear skies), drive or walk to the edge of town near the fjord for independent aurora viewing. The fjord's natural darkness makes it an excellent spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered from supermarket supplies — skyr, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot coffee and sandwiches from the hotel or local bakery to enjoy near Hofsós — budget ~1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel room if facilities allow, or dine at Hannes Boy — grilled Arctic char or lamb stew ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós pool admission is approximately 1,000–1,500 ISK. Bring a towel and swimsuit. The pool is heated year-round but wind chill can be intense — the contrast of warm water and cold air is part of the magic. The Emigration Centre may have limited winter hours; call ahead. Road conditions on Route 76 can be icy in January — check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike — drive through the Héðinsfjörðargöng tunnel (free) to reach the completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord. This hauntingly beautiful valley was abandoned in 1951 and the ruins of the old farmsteads remain. Hike along the fjord floor, exploring the ghostly remnants of the settlement surrounded by dramatic mountain walls. Allow 2–3 hours for the hike depending on snow conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return through the tunnel to Siglufjörður. Warm up at the hotel with hot drinks. In the afternoon, explore the upper reaches of Siglufjörður valley on foot or by car — the ski slopes of Skarðsdalur are nearby and offer a glimpse of the dramatic terrain. If conditions allow, take a short snowshoe walk (rental available locally) along the valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in town. Visit the local swimming pool again for a soak in the hot pots. Then enjoy dinner at the hotel restaurant or Hannes Boy. Check aurora forecasts — if clear, position yourself at the harbour or fjord edge for viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs, skyr, bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and energy bars for the Héðinsfjörður hike — self-catered ~1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — try the catch of the day or traditional Icelandic lamb ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is weather-dependent — in heavy snow or ice, the terrain can be challenging. Wear waterproof boots with good grip and bring trekking poles if available. The tunnel to Héðinsfjörður is single-lane with passing places — drive slowly and use headlights. This is one of Iceland's most atmospheric and undervisited spots. No facilities whatsoever in the fjord.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Dalvík (approximately 1 hour via the Ólafsfjörður tunnel) for the Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari. Board a whale watching vessel from Dalvík harbour — humpback whales, minke whales, and white-beaked dolphins are frequently spotted in these waters even in winter. The dramatic Tröllaskagi mountains rising from the sea make for a spectacular backdrop. Tours typically run 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the sea safari, explore Dalvík briefly — visit the Hvoll Museum which houses the famous 'Giant of Dalvík' exhibit. Have lunch in town before driving back north. Stop at Ólafsfjörður on the return journey to walk the small harbour and admire the steep mountain walls that almost completely enclose this tiny town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Rest and warm up. Evening aurora hunt — either join another guided tour or self-drive to a dark spot along the fjord. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance area offers excellent dark skies with no light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the drive to Dalvík
meals.lunch: Gísli, Eiríkur, Helgi restaurant in Dalvík — a beloved local spot known for excellent fish and chips and lamb dishes ~3,000–4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at the hotel or light meal at Kaffi Rauðka — soup and bread ~2,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Book the whale watching tour in advance through Arctic Sea Tours or Whale Watching Dalvík — prices approximately 10,000–12,000 ISK per person. Dress in extreme layers for the boat — the wind chill at sea in January is severe. The operator provides overalls. Sea sickness medication recommended if prone. Confirm the tour runs in winter as schedules vary.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri (approximately 1.5 hours south via Route 82 and Route 1). Explore Iceland's second city — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill above town, with its striking modernist architecture and panoramic views over Eyjafjörður. Walk the pedestrianised Hafnarstræti shopping street and browse local boutiques and bookshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for rotating exhibitions of Icelandic contemporary art — a cultural contrast to the natural landscapes. Then head to the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, beautiful even in winter with its snow-covered structures. Stop at the Netto or Krónan supermarket to restock supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at one of Akureyri's excellent mid-range restaurants before driving back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, consider staying in Akureyri overnight if a special aurora forecast warrants exploring the Eyjafjörður area — but return to Hotel Siglunes is the plan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café on Hafnarstræti, Akureyri — a classic Icelandic café with soups, sandwiches, and excellent coffee ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Rub23 restaurant in Akureyri — excellent sushi and grilled meats, mid-range ~4,000–6,000 ISK, or Strikið for panoramic fjord views

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip offering urban amenities, shopping, and cultural experiences. Stock up on any supplies you need — it's the largest town in the region. The drive back to Siglufjörður in the dark requires care on potentially icy mountain roads. Check road.is before the return journey. Akureyri also has a geothermal swimming pool worth a quick visit.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or exploring Siglufjörður's small but charming streets at a slow pace. Visit the local bakery for fresh pastries and coffee. Browse the small craft and souvenir shops near the harbour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Hofsós Infinity Pool for a second visit — this time focus on the meditative experience of soaking in geothermal water while watching the winter light fade over Skagafjörður. The golden hour light (around 13:00–14:30 in January) creates extraordinary colours over the fjord. Bring a camera. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — second guided aurora tour. With a week of experience reading the local conditions, you'll be better positioned to appreciate the hunt. The guide will take you to new locations along the fjord. Afterwards, warm up with hot chocolate at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — daily soup special and fresh bread ~2,000–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — try something different from the menu, perhaps the Arctic char with local herbs ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: A mid-trip rest day is important on a 13-day itinerary, especially given the physical demands of hiking and cold weather activities. Use this day to recharge. The second Hofsós visit at a different time of day will offer a completely different atmosphere. January's brief daylight window means the golden hour is actually quite accessible in the early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive to explore the Skagafjörður region — head south on Route 76 past Hofsós toward Sauðárkrókur (approximately 1.5 hours). Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved traditional turf farmhouses, offering a vivid glimpse into how Icelanders lived for centuries. The snow-covered turf roofs in winter are particularly photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Varmahlíð and the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum for deeper context on the region's history. Then drive to the Reykir geothermal area — a natural hot spring area in the valley. Return north via a different route if road conditions allow, taking in the broad Skagafjörður valley with its horse farms (Icelandic horses are bred extensively here).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by early evening. Warm up at the hotel. Self-guided aurora watching from the hotel — the fjord's natural darkness is ideal. Set an alarm for 22:00–02:00 if the forecast is strong.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the drive
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær or packed lunch from the hotel — soup in a thermos and sandwiches ~1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel using supermarket supplies — pasta, local cheese, and Icelandic bread ~2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is open year-round but with reduced winter hours — confirm before visiting (typically 10:00–17:00). Admission approximately 2,000 ISK. The Skagafjörður valley is famous for Icelandic horse breeding — you may see herds in the snow-covered fields. Road conditions in the valley can be challenging in January; check road.is. This is a longer driving day — approximately 3–4 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the mountains above Siglufjörður on foot or by snowshoe. The Skarðsdalur ski area is a short drive from town — even non-skiers can enjoy the mountain environment. Walk the lower slopes and take in the extraordinary views down the fjord. The combination of snow-covered peaks, the dark fjord water, and the low winter sun creates unforgettable scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a long soak in the hot pots. Spend time chatting with locals — Icelanders are famously friendly at their pools. Then visit the Herring Era Museum again to explore any exhibits you may have missed on Day 2, or attend any special winter programming.
day_by_day.evening: Special dinner evening — treat yourself to the best meal of the trip at Hannes Boy, ordering the full tasting experience if available. Pair with local Icelandic craft beer or a glass of wine. Celebrate the halfway point of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up for the morning mountain walk
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or Kaffi Rauðka after the swim ~2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — splurge slightly on a multi-course meal with fresh local seafood and lamb ~6,000–8,000 ISK per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: The Skarðsdalur ski area is small but charming — if you ski or snowboard, day passes are available at reasonable prices (~5,000–7,000 ISK). Equipment rental is available. Even without skiing, the mountain scenery is worth the short drive. Check avalanche forecasts before venturing onto open slopes — January can bring significant snowfall.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Ólafsfjörður (approximately 20 minutes through the tunnel) for a different perspective on the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Walk the small harbour and explore the town, which is even more dramatically enclosed by mountains than Siglufjörður. Hike the lower slopes of the surrounding mountains for panoramic views — the terrain is wild and beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive further south to Grenivík on the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður (approximately 1.5 hours). Visit the Laufás turf farm — another beautifully preserved historic farmstead with a small church. The setting above the fjord is spectacular. Return north via Akureyri if needed for any supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by early evening. Northern lights conditions permitting, drive to the Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance for aurora viewing — this spot offers complete darkness and a wide sky view. Bring a tripod for long-exposure photography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and snacks for the day trip — self-catered ~1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy or self-catered at the hotel — simple but satisfying ~2,500–4,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Laufás is typically open in summer only — call ahead to confirm winter access. The exterior and grounds are always accessible. The drive around Eyjafjörður offers some of the most dramatic fjord scenery in Iceland. Fuel up in Akureyri if needed — petrol stations in smaller towns may have limited hours. Total driving today is approximately 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated photography and nature morning — rise before the brief winter dawn (around 10:30) and position yourself at the harbour or fjord edge to capture the extraordinary light as it illuminates the snow-covered mountains. The combination of pink and golden light on the peaks reflected in the dark fjord water is one of Iceland's most magical winter sights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final visit to the Hofsós Infinity Pool — this time bring a good book and spend a full 2 hours simply relaxing and reflecting on the trip. The geothermal warmth, the fjord views, and the silence make this one of the most restorative experiences in Iceland. Drive back to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — final guided aurora tour of the trip. With multiple nights of experience, you'll know exactly what to look for and how to photograph the lights. Celebrate any sightings with hot chocolate from the guide's thermos.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the dawn photography session — hotel or self-catered
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka — final visit to this local favourite ~2,000–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — order your favourite dish from the trip for a nostalgic final dinner ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January dawn in Siglufjörður is brief and extraordinarily beautiful — the low sun angle creates long shadows and intense colours on the snow. A wide-angle lens and tripod are ideal. The Hofsós pool is at its most peaceful on weekday afternoons. This is a good day to buy any final souvenirs — the Herring Era Museum shop has excellent local crafts and books.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — begin with a farewell walk through Siglufjörður, revisiting favourite spots: the harbour, the colourful houses, the museum waterfront. Take time to appreciate the extraordinary setting of this remote fjord town, one of the most northerly inhabited places in Iceland. Visit the local bakery one last time for pastries and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Akureyri for final shopping and errands — pick up Icelandic souvenirs (wool products, local spirits, dried fish, skyr products), visit the Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið) which is open year-round, and explore any shops you missed on Day 6. Have a final Akureyri lunch. Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Pack bags and prepare for departure. Final aurora watch from the hotel window or a short walk to the harbour — fingers crossed for one last display. Enjoy a quiet farewell dinner and reflect on 12 extraordinary days in the Icelandic north.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — final Icelandic café experience ~2,500–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy — final dinner in Siglufjörður, order something celebratory ~4,000–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið) in Akureyri is a unique year-round Christmas shop — a fun and quirky Icelandic experience. Stock up on duty-free items in Akureyri if needed. Confirm your departure logistics for the next morning — the drive to Keflavík is approximately 5–5.5 hours, so an early start is essential. Check road.is the night before for any road closures or weather warnings.

day_by_day.morning: Very early departure from Hotel Siglunes — aim to leave by 04:00–05:00 to allow sufficient time for the drive to Keflavík International Airport. The drive south via Route 1 through Akureyri, across the highland plateau (or coastal route depending on conditions), and down to the Reykjanes Peninsula takes approximately 5–5.5 hours. Drive carefully on potentially icy winter roads.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík Airport with time to spare. Return the rental car, check in, and clear security. Browse the duty-free shops — Icelandic wool products, Brennivín schnapps, and Skyr are popular purchases. Enjoy a final Icelandic meal at the airport before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Icelandic north — the aurora dancing over Siglufjörður, the geothermal warmth of Hofsós, the haunting silence of Héðinsfjörður, and the wild beauty of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at the hotel before departure — prepare the night before with hotel supplies
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station café en route (N1 or Olis near Akureyri or Borgarnes) — soup and sandwich ~2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant at Keflavík — Icelandic lamb or fish dish for a final taste of Iceland ~4,000–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: A 04:00 departure from Siglufjörður is necessary to safely reach Keflavík in time for most international flights. Set multiple alarms. The winter drive south can be challenging — check road.is the night before and morning of departure. If road conditions are severe (red or orange warnings), consider departing even earlier or exploring alternative routes. Fill the rental car with petrol before returning it. Keep all receipts for any insurance claims.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear immigration and collect luggage, then transfer via pre-arranged luxury private car service northward toward Siglufjörður (approximately 4–5 hours). Enjoy the dramatic winter landscape along Route 1 and the Tröllaskagi Peninsula roads as dawn breaks over the volcanic terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður mid-afternoon. Check in, settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord, and take a leisurely orientation stroll along the charming harbor front of this intimate fishing town. Rest and acclimatize after the overnight flight.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Hotel Siglunes' own restaurant or the acclaimed Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður, savoring locally sourced Arctic char, lamb, and Icelandic seafood. Early night to recover from travel and prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge before departure or en route at a roadside café stop
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic box arranged by the hotel driver, enjoyed en route with thermos coffee
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka, Siglufjörður — intimate candlelit dining featuring pan-seared Arctic char, slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank, and skyr panna cotta with crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer well in advance. The drive north includes the single-lane Héðinsfjarðargöng tunnel — the driver will be familiar with it. Pack layers; temperatures will be around 0–5°C on arrival. Hotel Siglunes should be notified of early/late check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore three beautifully restored warehouse buildings chronicling Siglufjörður's golden age as the herring capital of the North Atlantic, with immersive exhibits, restored boats, and period-accurate salt-fish processing stations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk along the Siglufjörður harbor and old town with a local cultural guide, visiting the restored old merchant houses, the tiny folk music museum, and the scenic viewpoints above the fjord. Stop for hot chocolate at a local café before returning to the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — join a guided aurora tour departing from the hotel, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from any light pollution. Your expert guide will use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud-cover data to find the best vantage points. Wrap up in hotel-provided thermal suits and sip hot cocoa under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — fish soup, open-faced langoustine sandwiches, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Pre-tour early dinner at Hotel Siglunes — reindeer carpaccio, pan-fried cod with beurre blanc, and warm lava cake with vanilla skyr ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — confirm opening times (typically 10:00–18:00 in summer, reduced in winter). Northern lights tours are weather-dependent; the guide will assess conditions by late afternoon. Aurora activity in January is statistically strong in northern Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula (approximately 45 minutes) to the village of Hofsós and visit the legendary Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool — widely regarded as Iceland's most beautifully situated geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge with panoramic views over Skagafjörður fjord. Soak in the 38–40°C geothermal waters as winter light plays across the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Hofsós, including the Icelandic Emigration Centre, which tells the story of 19th-century Icelanders who emigrated to North America. Browse the small local craft shops, then drive back toward Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road, stopping at dramatic fjord viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private in-room dining experience arranged by Hotel Siglunes, or dine at Kaffi Rauðka with a tasting menu of seasonal Icelandic ingredients paired with Icelandic craft beers and aquavit.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — freshly baked pastries, Icelandic yogurt, smoked trout, and pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light café lunch in Hofsós village — lamb soup, fresh bread, and coffee
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka tasting menu — five courses featuring local langoustine, smoked lamb, fermented shark (hákarl) amuse-bouche, and Icelandic cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós Pool is approximately 45 km south of Siglufjörður via Route 76. Bring swimwear and a towel (or rent on-site). The pool is heated year-round and is magical in winter — steam rising against snow-capped mountains. Road conditions in January may require caution; check Vegagerðin (road.is) before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike — drive through the Héðinsfjarðargöng tunnel (just minutes from Siglufjörður) and emerge into the completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord. With a local guide, hike through the hauntingly beautiful landscape past the ruins of the abandoned farm settlement, surrounded by towering mountains and absolute silence.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Héðinsfjörður's inner reaches, reaching the old farmstead ruins and the dramatic waterfall at the fjord's head. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch in this remote wilderness setting before returning through the tunnel to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at Hotel Siglunes. Book an in-hotel spa treatment or private hot tub session if available. Dinner at the hotel restaurant featuring a curated menu of Icelandic winter comfort food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full hot breakfast with eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and Icelandic rye bread
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch prepared by Hotel Siglunes — thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot coffee
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — slow-roasted leg of lamb with root vegetable gratin, followed by Icelandic rice pudding with cinnamon and rhubarb jam

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is approximately 8–12 km round trip depending on route. Wear waterproof hiking boots and full winter layers. The tunnel is free to use. In January, daylight is limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so an early start around 10:00 is recommended. A local guide is strongly advised for safety and historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður (approximately 30–45 minutes south) for the Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari. Board a premium small-group vessel and explore the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður, one of Iceland's longest fjords, in search of humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and seabirds. Thermal suits and hot drinks provided on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to port and explore the small town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður. Visit the quirky Byggðasafnið Hvoll folk museum in Dalvík (home to the famous 'Giant of Dalvík' exhibit). Enjoy a warm lunch before the scenic drive back to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunting excursion from Siglufjörður — a second attempt maximizes aurora viewing chances. Your guide will select a different dark-sky location based on that evening's forecast, potentially venturing further into the Tröllaskagi highlands for unobstructed views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — skyr parfait, Icelandic pancakes with crowberry jam, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn restaurant in Dalvík — hearty fish and chips, lobster bisque, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Hotel Siglunes before the aurora tour — grilled Arctic char with dill butter, potato gratin, and a selection of Icelandic cheeses

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching tours in January operate weather and sea-condition permitting. Arctic Adventures and Whale Watching Dalvík are reputable operators. Book in advance. Sea conditions in January can be rough — motion sickness medication is advisable if sensitive. The tour typically lasts 2.5–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at Hotel Siglunes. Sleep in after the late aurora tour. Enjoy a late breakfast and spend the morning exploring Siglufjörður's charming streets at your own pace — browse the small local shops, visit the tiny Siglufjörður church, and photograph the colorful harbor houses reflected in the still fjord waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing or winter hiking excursion on the slopes above Siglufjörður with a local mountain guide. The town is surrounded by dramatic peaks and ridges that offer spectacular views over the fjord and surrounding mountains in the brief winter daylight. This area is also famous for its avalanche history — your guide will provide full safety briefing.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef dinner experience arranged through Hotel Siglunes — a local Icelandic chef prepares a bespoke multi-course meal in the hotel's private dining space, featuring the finest seasonal ingredients: langoustine, reindeer, skyr desserts, and Icelandic wines and spirits.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — eggs any style, smoked lamb, fresh pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a local café — lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Private chef multi-course dinner at Hotel Siglunes — amuse-bouche of smoked trout mousse, langoustine bisque, reindeer tenderloin with juniper jus, Icelandic cheese course, and skyr soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Siglufjörður sits in a narrow fjord valley and is one of Iceland's most avalanche-prone areas. Always hike with a local guide in winter and check avalanche forecasts at vedur.is. The private chef dinner should be arranged 48 hours in advance with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula to the town of Sauðárkrókur (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður) — the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum and explore the town's Viking-age heritage. The region is famous for its Icelandic horse breeding tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Icelandic horse riding experience on the famous Tölt gait — arrange a premium guided ride through the snow-dusted Skagafjörður landscape with one of the region's top horse farms. The Icelandic horse's unique fifth gait makes for an exceptionally smooth and memorable winter ride.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sauðárkrókur at Kaffi Krókur or Hotel Mikligarður before the scenic drive back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, arrange for a late return and dine at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic spread with smoked fish, rye bread, skyr, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Sauðárkrókur café — traditional Icelandic meat soup (kjötsúpa) and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Kaffi Krókur, Sauðárkrókur — pan-seared lamb fillet, roasted root vegetables, and Icelandic dessert platter, or return to Hotel Siglunes for dinner

day_by_day.notes: Sauðárkrókur is approximately 60 km from Siglufjörður via Route 76 and Route 75. Road conditions in January require careful driving — check road.is. Horse riding farms in the area include Hestur.is affiliated farms; book in advance. Rides typically last 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Return visit to the Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool for a longer, more meditative soak — this time arriving at opening time to enjoy the pool in the early winter light before crowds arrive. Spend 2–3 hours in the geothermal waters, alternating between the main pool and cold plunge, practicing the traditional Nordic bathing ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive further south to explore the Skagafjörður coastline and the historic Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved 18th-century turf farmsteads, offering a vivid window into traditional Icelandic rural life. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal route.
day_by_day.evening: Third Northern Lights Hunting attempt from Siglufjörður — with three attempts over the 13-day trip, the statistical probability of witnessing the aurora is very high. This evening, your guide may take you to a high-elevation viewpoint above the fjord for a 360-degree aurora panorama.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from the hotel, enjoyed at Glaumbær or en route
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — early dinner before the aurora tour: pan-fried haddock with capers and lemon butter, followed by warm Icelandic doughnuts (kleinar) with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm museum may have limited winter hours or be closed in January — verify in advance at nat.is. The Hofsós pool is open year-round. January aurora activity peaks around new moon periods — check aurora forecast at en.vedur.is for optimal viewing nights.

day_by_day.morning: Ice fishing experience on a frozen lake or river in the Tröllaskagi Peninsula interior, arranged through a local guide. Learn traditional Icelandic ice fishing techniques, drill through the ice, and try your luck catching Arctic char or trout in pristine wilderness conditions. A truly unique and exclusive winter activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þórbergssetur) and attend or arrange a private performance of traditional Icelandic folk music — the town has a rich musical heritage. Alternatively, take a photography walk along the harbor with a local photographer guide to capture the dramatic winter light and colorful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Hotel Siglunes. Enjoy the hotel's facilities, read by the fire, and have a leisurely dinner. If the sky is clear, step outside independently to watch for the aurora — the hotel's fjordside location offers excellent dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full hot breakfast with Icelandic oatmeal, smoked lamb, eggs, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Streamside gourmet packed lunch during the ice fishing excursion — thermos of soup, artisan sandwiches, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — slow-cooked Icelandic lamb with root vegetable purée, followed by skyr cheesecake with blueberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing requires a local guide and appropriate licensing — arrange through the hotel concierge. The experience is highly weather and ice-condition dependent. Dress in maximum thermal layers. The folk music centre may require advance booking for private performances.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður via the Ólafsfjörður tunnel). Explore the charming city center, visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched above the town, and browse the excellent Akureyri Art Museum and the Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn), the world's northernmost botanical garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri's premium shopping and dining scene. Visit the Geysir shop for high-quality Icelandic woolens and design goods. Stroll along Hafnarstræti, the main pedestrian street, and visit the Christmas House (Jólahúsið) — open year-round and particularly magical in January.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before the drive back to Siglufjörður. Rub23 is widely regarded as the best restaurant in northern Iceland, offering an exceptional sushi and grill menu with premium Icelandic ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri — traditional Icelandic lamb soup, fish of the day, and Icelandic desserts in a cozy historic setting
meals.dinner: Rub23, Akureyri — premium omakase sushi selection, grilled Arctic char, wagyu beef, and a curated cocktail menu featuring Icelandic spirits

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 65 km from Siglufjörður via Route 82 and the Vaðlaheiðargöng tunnel. The drive is scenic but requires winter driving caution. Rub23 is very popular — book well in advance. Allow time for the return drive in darkness; the road is well-maintained but can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile or snowcat tour in the mountains above Siglufjörður or the Tröllaskagi highlands — arrange through a specialist local operator for an exhilarating ride across pristine snowfields with panoramic views of the fjords below. This is one of the most thrilling winter activities available in the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and visit the Herring Era Museum for a deeper dive — arrange a private guided tour with the museum curator for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience, including access to the museum's archive and private collection of historical photographs and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at Kaffi Rauðka — order the chef's special tasting menu and pair with a selection of Icelandic craft spirits. Reflect on the journey so far over a long, leisurely meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — smoked fish platter, rye bread, skyr with honey, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel after the snowmobile tour — warming lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka chef's tasting menu — seven courses featuring the best of Icelandic winter produce, paired with Brennivín aquavit, Icelandic craft beer, and imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours require a valid driving license and a safety briefing. Minimum age restrictions apply. Book through Arctic Adventures or a local Siglufjörður operator. The private museum tour should be arranged through the hotel concierge at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final Héðinsfjörður exploration — return to the abandoned fjord for a different route, this time focusing on photography and quiet contemplation. The winter light in Héðinsfjörður is extraordinary, with low-angle golden hour light lasting most of the brief day. Bring a professional camera or arrange a photography guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður for a final afternoon of leisure. Visit any remaining local spots — the small harbor, the old fish factory ruins, the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjörður) for a final geothermal soak. Pack and prepare for departure the following day.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at Hotel Siglunes — arrange a special private dining experience with the hotel, celebrating the end of an extraordinary 13-day Icelandic adventure. Request a window table overlooking the fjord. If conditions allow, the hotel staff can alert you to any aurora activity for one final viewing from the hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full celebratory breakfast with all the Icelandic classics
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Siglufjörður café — fish soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Private farewell dinner at Hotel Siglunes — bespoke menu created by the chef: langoustine cocktail, reindeer tartare, pan-roasted halibut with saffron cream, Icelandic cheese board, and skyr brûlée with crowberry sorbet, paired with Champagne and Icelandic spirits

day_by_day.notes: Pack the evening before to allow a relaxed final morning. Confirm the private airport transfer for the following day. The hotel concierge can arrange luggage storage if needed. Request a late checkout if the flight schedule allows.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður — wake early for one last walk along the harbor in the pre-dawn darkness, watching for the aurora or the first hints of winter sunrise over the fjord peaks. Enjoy a final full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes, savoring every last bite of smoked fish, skyr, and fresh rye bread.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Hotel Siglunes and depart via private luxury transfer southward to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 4.5–5 hours). The drive south offers a final panoramic showcase of Iceland's dramatic winter landscape — volcanic plains, glacier glimpses, and the vast North Atlantic coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík Airport with ample time before departure. Access the premium Icelandair Saga Lounge for a final Icelandic meal and drinks before boarding. Depart Iceland carrying extraordinary memories of the aurora, the hot springs, the silent fjords, and the warmth of the north.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — the complete Icelandic spread, enjoyed slowly
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch for the road, or stop at a premium roadside restaurant en route south
meals.dinner: Icelandair Saga Lounge at Keflavík Airport — premium lounge dining with Icelandic specialties and a farewell glass of Brennivín or Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 5 hours for the drive from Siglufjörður to Keflavík in January — road conditions, weather, and reduced daylight can extend journey time. Check road.is before departure. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before your flight. Confirm the private transfer the evening before. Duty-free shopping at Keflavík is excellent for Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and woolens.
